words.gram: m. nom. pl. (e before a vowel)

hindi: ये सोम दही से मिश्रित होकर इन्द्र के लिए निचोड़े गए हैं। हे वज्र-हस्त, उन्हें पीने के लिए, हर्ष के लिए, अपने दो हरे घोड़ों के साथ अपने निवास से आओ।
english: These Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for Indra. O thunderbolt-handed one, come with your two bay horses from your abode to them, to drink them for exhilaration.
notes: tā~ is read as tān (anunāsika standing for n before ā). yāhyoka ā is read yāhi + okaḥ ā 'come to the abode'; it could also be yāhi + oke ā (locative, 'in the abode'); the sense is the same. The relative reading 'to them' (tān) refers back to the Soma juices.

words.gram: m. nom. pl. (e before a vowel)
pf. part. mid. √pā, m. nom. sg.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, ये सोम स्तुतियों के साथ तुम्हारे हर्ष के लिए प्रकट हैं। मधुर रस को पीकर हमारी स्तुतियों को सुनो; हे स्तुतिप्रिय, स्तोता को दो।
english: O Indra, these Soma juices, accompanied by recitations, are ready for your exhilaration. Having drunk of the sweet drink, listen to our songs; give to the singer, O lover of songs.

text_flags.why: possible: cikitra is not a clear form as printed; the sense wants a verb for somāḥ (are known / appear).
possible: the printed word has i and a transposed; ukthinaḥ 'with recitations' is the expected form.

notes: Both somāścikitra and ukithanaḥ are doubtful; the translation follows the corrected readings. If cikitra is instead a vocative, the line would address a 'wise one' (compare cikitvas in the glossary), but no such form is clear.

hindi: आज मैं तुम्हें बुलाता हूँ, जो सबरदुघा, अर्थात् अमृत-तुल्य रस देने वाले और गायत्र गान से कम्पित होने वाले हो; इन्द्र को, उत्तम दुहने योग्य गाय को, दूसरे अन्न को, विस्तृत धाराओं वाले और भली-भाँति तैयार किए हुए को भी बुलाता हूँ।
english: Today I call you, the one who yields sabar (a nectar-like drink), stirred by the gāyatra song; Indra, the good-milking cow, another refreshment with broad streams, made ready.

text_flags.why: the 3 is a pluta (prolongation) mark in singing; no change to the words.

notes: The line is obscure and its grammar is uncertain. sabardughā~ is read as sabardughām (acc. sg. f.) agreeing with tvā or with dhenum; sabar is a rare word for a nectar-like milk or drink, not certain. The last long token is one printed word that joins five words (sudughām anyām iṣam urudhārām araṅkṛtam). The 'cow' language is figurative for what Indra yields. Translation is tentative.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, बड़े पत्थर और दृढ़ शक्तियाँ तुम्हें रोक नहीं सकतीं, जब तुम मुझ जैसे स्तोता को धन देना चाहते हो; तुम्हारे उस दान को कोई नष्ट नहीं करता।
english: Neither the great stones nor the strong ones can hold you back, O Indra, when you wish to give wealth to a praiser like me; no one diminishes that gift of yours.
notes: kiṣṭadā is read as kiḥ (as in na kiḥ 'no one') + tat + ā, with ā going with mināti ('ā mināti'); the line is obscure. adrayaḥ may be 'mountains' or 'pressing stones'; vīḍavaḥ is taken as an adjective of the stones ('firm') but could stand alone.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. mid. √mand

hindi: सोम के निचोड़े जाने पर साथ पीते हुए उसे कौन जानता है? उसने कौन-सा बल धारण किया है? यह वही है जो अपने ओज से नगरों को तोड़ देता है, सोमरस से आनन्दित होने वाला शिप्री।
english: Who knows him as he drinks together at the pressing? What vigour has he taken? This is he who breaks open the strongholds with his might, rejoicing, the fair-lipped one, in the Soma juice.
notes: kadvayo is read kat vayaḥ 'what vigour'. śipri is taken as a nominative epithet (fair-lipped or helmeted), a doubtful word; the line is about Indra though the verse does not name him.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, जब तुम नियमहीन शत्रु को दण्ड दो, तो उसे उसके स्थान से हटा दो। हे मघवन्, हमारे बहुतों से चाहे गए अंश को धन में बढ़ाओ।
english: When, O Indra, you chastise the lawless one, drive him away from his seat. Our share, O Maghavan, desired by many, make great in wealth.
notes: aṃśu may be 'share/portion' or the Soma-stalk; the translation takes 'share'. sadasaspari is read as sadasaḥ pari 'from the seat'. adhi barhaya is 'raise up/enlarge'.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (name of a god)
m. nom. sg. (name of a god)

words.gloss: Brahmaṇaspati, lord of the sacred word

words.gram: f. nom. sg. (name of a goddess)

hindi: त्वष्टा, पर्जन्य और ब्रह्मणस्पति हमारी दिव्य वाणी को धारण करें। पुत्रों और भाइयों के साथ अदिति अब हमारी रक्षा करे; हमारी वाणी दुर्जेय और रक्षा करने वाली हो।
english: May Tvaṣṭṛ, Parjanya and Brahmaṇaspati attend to our divine word. May Aditi, with sons and brothers, now protect us; the word is hard to overcome and protecting.
notes: The sentence is elliptical: the first line has no verb of its own, and the translation supplies 'attend to' (or the verb pātu of the second line carries over to the first line). duṣṭaraṃ trāmaṇaṃ vacaḥ is taken as a closing phrase; its link is not clear.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम कभी बाँझ नहीं हो; तुम दानी भक्त को देते हो। हे मघवन्, निकट से निकट, और अधिक, तुम देवता का दान दिया जाता है।
english: Never are you barren, O Indra; you bestow on the worshipper. Nearer and nearer, O Maghavan, ever more is the gift of you, the god, bestowed.
notes: kadā ca na is the printed spelling of kadā cana 'ever' (the editors print it as three tokens). starī is a barren cow, here a figure for withholding. upopennu is read upa upa it nu 'nearer and nearer, indeed now'; the sense of pṛcyate (mingled, bestowed) is not certain.

hindi: हे वृत्रहन्ताओं में श्रेष्ठ इन्द्र, दूर से अपने दो हरे घोड़ों को जोतो। हे मघवन्, हमारी ओर मुड़कर, हे उग्र, सोम पीने के लिए ऊँचे घोड़ों के साथ आओ।
english: Yoke your two bay horses, O Indra, best slayer of Vṛtra, from afar. Turned towards us, O Maghavan, mighty one, come with your lofty steeds to drink Soma.
notes: ṛṣvebhiḥ is taken as 'with the lofty (horses)', supplying the noun.

hindi: हे वज्रधारी, कल और आज उत्साही मनुष्यों ने तुम्हें ही बढ़ाया है। हे इन्द्र, तुम यहाँ स्तोत्र ले आने वाले की पुकार सुनो और घर आओ।
english: Yesterday and now the eager men have made you swell, O wielder of the thunderbolt. You, Indra, here hear the hymn-bearer, and come to the home.
notes: tvāmidā hyo is read tvām idā hyaḥ 'you now (and) yesterday'; the line is obscure and the reading of idā hyaḥ is tentative. stomavāhasa is taken as a genitive singular of stoma-vāhas ('of the one who carries the hymn').

words.gram: f. nom. sg., pres. part. ā-√i
f. nom. sg., pres. part. ud-√vas

hindi: आकाश की पुत्री, उदय होती हुई, आती हुई दिखाई दी है। वह महान उषा अंधकार को दूर हटाती है कि आँख देख सके, और वह उदार देवी प्रकाश करती है।
english: The daughter of heaven, dawning as she comes, has been seen. The great one opens up the darkness to the eye, and the bountiful one makes light.
notes: The 3 in āyatyū3cchantī is a pluta (prolongation) mark in the chant, placed here after ucchantī. The subject is the dawn (Uṣas), who is not named in the verse; the translation keeps the epithets. apo is read apa u.

hindi: हे चमकीले अश्विनो, ये यज्ञ-आह्वान तुम दोनों को पुकारते हैं। मैं भी रक्षा के लिए तुम दोनों को बुलाता हूँ, हे शक्ति के धनी; क्योंकि तुम दोनों हर बस्ती में जाते हो।
english: O bright Aśvins, these heavenward rites call you two. I too call you two for help, O rich in power, for you go to every clan.
notes: diviṣṭayaḥ is rendered 'heavenward rites'; the exact sense ('invocations', 'sacrifices at dawn') varies. The Aśvins are two divine physician twins named only in vocative.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. √tap, m. nom. sg.
m. nom. du. or inst. sg. (uncertain)

hindi: तुम दोनों कहाँ हो? हे अश्विनो, कौन मनुष्य तपता हुआ है, हे देवो? पत्थर से कूटता हुआ, सोम के डण्ठल से इस प्रकार तुम दोनों को तपाता है।
english: Where are you two? What mortal, O Aśvins, is suffering, O gods? Striking with the stone, wearing down with the Soma-stalk, thus he troubles you.
notes: The second line is very obscure and its grammar uncertain: ghnatā, kṣapamāṇo~, and ādunyathā are doubtful readings, and the printed ṣṭhaḥ (for sthaḥ) after ku is a sandhi spelling. The translation is a tentative reading only, needs review.

hindi: यह अत्यन्त मधुर सोम तुम दोनों के लिए यज्ञों में निचोड़ा गया है। हे अश्विनो, उसे दिन की अवधि बीतने पर पियो, और दानी भक्त को रत्न दो।
english: This sweetest Soma has been pressed for you two in the heavenward rites. Drink it, O Aśvins, (as kept over) from the day, and bestow treasures on the worshipper.
notes: tiro ahnyam is obscure ('kept over the day' or 'of the day aside'); rendered tentatively. dhatta~ is read dhattam (anunāsika for m before r).

hindi: सोम के कण्ठ-घूँट से मैं सदा याचना करता हुआ तुम्हें पुकारता हूँ; सवनों में जंगली पशु के समान उत्सुक और क्रुद्ध तुम स्वामी से कौन याचना न करे?
english: With the gulping of Soma I, always begging, (call) to you, eager like a wild beast roused at the pressings. Who would not beg of the lord?
notes: This verse is obscure. galdayā is of uncertain sense (gulping, swallowing); jyā is not understood and is kept as printed; the sentence has no clear main verb in line 1. Translation is tentative and must be reviewed.

hindi: हे अध्वर्यु, तुम सोम को बहाओ; इन्द्र पीना चाहता है। उसने अब निश्चय ही अपने दो बलवान हरे घोड़े जोत लिए हैं और वृत्रहन्ता आ गया है।
english: O Adhvaryu, make the Soma flow; Indra wishes to drink. Surely he has now yoked his two virile bay horses, and the slayer of Vṛtra has come.
notes: tva~ is tvam (anunāsika for m). vṛṣṇā is taken as the dual vṛṣaṇā (a Vedic shortened spelling), agreeing with harī.

words.gloss: of the existing, of the one who is

hindi: हे इन्द्र, छोटे के लिए उस बड़े धन को लाओ। हे मघवन्, तुम बहुत धन वाले हुए हो और हर युद्ध में पुकारे जाने योग्य हो।
english: Bring that, O Indra, the greater (wealth) to the lesser one. For you, O Maghavan, have become rich in much wealth, and you are to be invoked in every battle.
notes: The first line is obscure. abhī ṣatas is read abhi sataḥ; the translation takes jyāyaḥ kanīyasaḥ as 'greater (wealth) for the lesser (man)' but the construction is uncertain.

words.gloss: I would give up, I would surrender

hindi: हे इन्द्र, जितने का तुम स्वामी हो, उतने का मैं स्वामी होता तो हे धन देने वाले, मैं स्तोता को अवश्य सँभालता और उसे दुर्गति के हवाले न करता।
english: If I were lord, O Indra, of as much as you are, I would indeed support the singer, O giver of wealth, and would not surrender him to wretchedness.

text_flags.why: possible: the form printed is the 2 sg. pres. mid.; the sense wants a first-person conditional, but the printed form may be an edition reading with ellipsis.

notes: The form dadhiṣe is formally 2 sg. mid. 'you uphold' or 1 sg. 'I uphold'; the translation takes the conditional 'I would support', following the sense of the verse. radāvaso is taken as radā-vaso (rada = giving; uncertain). raṃsiṣam is tentative (aor. of √ram 'to cause to rest, give up').

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम संघर्षों में सब शत्रुओं पर भारी हो। तुम निन्दा के नाशक, जनक और वृत्र को जीतने वाले हो; तुम हमला करने वालों को परास्त करो।
english: You, O Indra, are above all rivals in the onslaughts. You are the destroyer of ill-repute, the begetter, the conqueror of Vṛtra; overcome those who assail us.
notes: tūrya is taken as imperative of √tur; taruṣyataḥ as accusative plural 'those who wish to overcome'. aśasti can be 'curse, ill-repute, calumny'; rendered 'ill-repute'.

hindi: जो अपने बल से आकाश के आसनों से भी आगे निकल गया है, हे इन्द्र, पृथ्वी का लोक तुम्हें समा नहीं सकता; तुम सब कुछ से बढ़कर बढ़े हो।
english: He who has gone beyond the seats of heaven by his might, the earthly space does not contain you, O Indra; you have grown beyond everything.
notes: ririkṣa is printed with final a; it is taken as ririkṣe/ririkṣa 'has surpassed' (3 sg. pf. of √ric), the form is not certain. 'He who' in line 1 is Indra, addressed in line 2.

words.gloss: we would awaken, we would make mindful

hindi: दिव्य, दूध मिला सोमरस निचोड़ा गया है; इन्द्र ने जन्म से ही इसके विषय में कहा है। हे हरे घोड़ों के स्वामी, हम यज्ञों से तुम्हें जगाते हैं; सोम के आनन्द में हमारी स्तुति पर ध्यान दो।
english: The divine Soma juice mixed with milk has been pressed; Indra, from his birth, has spoken of it. We rouse you with sacrifices, O lord of bay horses; take note of our praise in the exhilarations of the Soma.
notes: Line 1 is obscure: the case of andhaḥ, the force of ni ... uvoca (ni-√vac 'declare') and the antecedent of asmin are uncertain. na in line 2 is read naḥ (the printed form lacks the visarga). goṛjīkam: ṛjīka is of doubtful sense ('mixed', 'shining').

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम्हारा आसन घर में बनाया गया है; हे बहुतों से पुकारे गए, मनुष्यों के साथ उसकी ओर आओ, ताकि तुम हमारे रक्षक, बढ़ाने वाले और धन देने वाले बनो और सोमों से आनन्दित हो।
english: Your seat has been made in the abode, O Indra; come forth to it with the men, O much-invoked, so that you may be our protector, our increaser and giver of riches, and rejoice with the Soma juices.
notes: dadaḥ and mamadaḥ are doubtful forms; the translation takes them as nominative participial epithets of Indra. Lines 1 and 2 are one sentence of invitation with purpose.

words.gram: m. acc. pl., pf. part. pass. √bādh

words.gloss: you set at rest, you made flow

hindi: तुमने स्रोत को फोड़ा और नालियाँ खोल दीं; रुकी हुई बाढ़ों को तुमने शान्त किया। हे इन्द्र, जब तुमने महान पर्वत से उन जलों को छोड़ा, तब धाराएँ बहीं, जब तुमने दानवों को मारा।
english: You broke open the spring and released the channels; you set at rest the confined floods. When, O Indra, you released you (the waters) from the great mountain, the streams (flowed) when you struck down the Dānavas.
notes: The second line is obscure: vaḥ (you, the waters), sṛjat (3 sg. injunctive or 2 sg. in -t) and the clause order are uncertain. aramṇāḥ is tentative (set at rest / made flow). The translation is a tentative reading, needs review.

words.gram: pf. part. mid. √su, m. nom. pl.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, सोम निचोड़ चुके हम वाज अर्थात् बल और पुरस्कार पाने की इच्छा से तुम्हारी स्तुति करते हैं, हे महान पौरुष वाले। हमारे लिए कल्याण लाओ; तुम्हारी सहायता से हम स्वयं और सन्तान के साथ विजयी हों।
english: We who have pressed (Soma) praise you, O Indra, desiring to win the prize, O you of great manly strength. Bring us well-being, which ..., that we may prevail, ourselves and with our offspring, helped by you.

text_flags.why: possible: konā is not a clear word here; the parallel Ṛgveda line has yasya cākan 'whose (good) he desires'. Kept as printed, not applied.

notes: konā is unresolved; the clause 'yasya konā' (of which ...) cannot be read with certainty, so its meaning is left blank in the translation. tanā tmanā are read as instrumentals 'by offspring, by ourselves'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, धन की चाह रखने वाले हमने तुम्हारा दाहिना हाथ पकड़ा है, हे धनों के स्वामी। हे शूर, हम तुम्हें गायों का स्वामी जानते हैं; हमें चमकता हुआ, भरपूर धन दो।
english: We have grasped your right hand, O Indra, desiring riches, O lord of riches. For we know you, O hero, as lord of cattle; give us brilliant, abundant wealth.
notes: gopati~ and vṛṣaṇa~ are read with anunāsika for m (gopatim, vṛṣaṇam). rayindāḥ is rayim + dāḥ (m changes to n before d in the print).

hindi: मनुष्य संग्राम में इन्द्र को पुकारते हैं, जब वे पार लगाने वाली उन स्तुतियों को जोड़ते हैं। हे शूर, मनुष्यों को जीतने और यश की इच्छा में गायों से भरे बाड़े में हमें भाग दो।
english: Men call upon Indra in the contest, when they yoke those prayers that carry across. O hero, in the winning of men and the desire for fame, give us a share in the cattle-rich pen.

text_flags.why: possible: the middle form havante is expected in the parallel verse; havanti (active) is also grammatical, so only a possible variant.

notes: nemadhitā (loc. sg. 'in the contest') is a tentative reading. kāma ā is read kāme ā; the alternative is kāmaḥ ā (nominative 'desire'). The 'pen' is figurative (a place full of cattle).

words.gram: m. nom. pl., bahuvrīhi (a clan name)
pres. part. mid., m. nom. pl.

words.gloss: with a fetter, in a bond

hindi: पक्षियों की तरह, सुन्दर पंखों वाले बाज़ों की तरह, प्रियमेध ऋषि प्रार्थना करते हुए इन्द्र के पास बैठे: अन्धकार को हटाओ, दृष्टि भर दो, और हमें, जो मानो बन्धन में बँधे हैं, मुक्त करो।
english: Like birds, like eagles, the sages of Priyamedha's clan sat near Indra, entreating: remove the darkness, fill our sight, and free us who are bound as if in a fetter.
notes: vayaḥ suparṇāḥ is taken as 'like birds, like eagles' (the verse does not use iva here); this is a tentative reading. The 3 in mumugdhyā3smān is a pluta mark on the first syllable of asmān and is listed after it. nidhayā (fetter) is uncertain.

hindi: जब तुम सुन्दर पंखों वाले को आकाश में ऊपर उड़ते देखकर, हृदय से चाहते हुए लोगों ने तुम्हें देखा, सोने के पंखों वाले, वरुण के दूत, यम के स्थान में पक्षी, तीव्र गति वाले को।
english: When, yearning with their hearts, they beheld you, the well-winged one, flying up in the vault of heaven, the golden-winged messenger of Varuṇa, the bird in the seat of Yama, the swift one.
notes: The verse does not name the one addressed (tvā); the translation keeps the epithets and does not identify him. patanta~ is patantam (anunāsika for m).

words.gram: pf. part. mid., n. acc. sg.

words.gloss: from the front, from the east

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (a name or epithet)

hindi: सुन्दर चमकने वाले वेन ने आगे की ओर से, सीमा से, पहले उत्पन्न ब्रह्म को और उजले स्थानों को खोल दिया। उसने अपने निकटतम गहरे स्थानों को और सत् तथा असत् की योनि को खोल दिया।
english: Vena, the bright one, from the front, from the boundary, opened the first-born sacred word and the bright places. He opened his nearest depths and the womb of what exists and of what does not exist.
notes: Vena is kept as printed (name or epithet 'the yearning one'); the verse does not give the later identification. brahma can be 'sacred word' or 'the Brahman'; rendered 'sacred word'. The grammar of line 1 (what Vena opened) is uncertain: brahma jajñānam and surucaḥ are both taken as objects.

hindi: इस महान वीर, बलवान और तीव्र, प्रचुर वज्रधारी, पुराने के लिए उन्होंने अनोखे, बहुत सारे और अत्यन्त कल्याणकारी वचन गढ़े हैं।
english: For this great hero, strong and swift, for the abundant wielder of the thunderbolt, the ancient one, they have fashioned new, most numerous and most beneficial words.
notes: vacā~syāsmai is read vacāṃsi asmai (the printed ā of syāsmai is a sandhi spelling); the verse does not name the god. sthavirāya may also be 'firm, steadfast'.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. √i, m. nom. sg.

hindi: काला बूँद दस हजार के साथ आगे बढ़ता हुआ अंशुमती नदी पर उतरा। साँस फूँकते हुए उसे इन्द्र ने अपनी शक्ति से सहारा दिया; पुरुषार्थी ने हथियार दूर कर दिया।
english: The black drop, advancing with ten thousand, stood down on the Aṃśumatī. Indra, manly-minded, withstood him as he blew, with his might, and put the weapon away.

text_flags.why: possible: the Ṛgveda parallel reads apa snīhitiṃ nṛmaṇā adhatta; adhadrāḥ is not a clear form.

notes: A tentative reading only: āvat may be 'helped' or 'withstood'; snīhiti is of doubtful sense (weapon, stroke); adhadrāḥ is unresolved, kept as printed and glossed from the Ṛgveda parallel. The drop (drapsa) is not interpreted. Needs review.

words.gram: pres. part. mid., m. nom. pl.

hindi: वृत्र की फुफकार से डरकर सब देवताओं ने, जो तुम्हारे मित्र थे, तुम्हें छोड़ दिया। हे इन्द्र, मरुतों के साथ तुम्हारी मित्रता हो; तब तुम इन सब सेनाओं को जीतोगे।
english: Fearing the snorting of Vṛtra, all the gods who were your friends abandoned you. Let there be friendship for you with the Maruts, O Indra; then you will conquer all these hosts.
notes: The Maruts are the storm-gods, named in the line as allies. The subject of the first verb is viśve devāḥ ye sakhāyaḥ.

words.gram: pres. part. mid., m. acc. sg.

hindi: अनेकों के समूह में दौड़ते हुए अकेले युवक को बूढ़े ने निगल लिया। देवता की काव्य-शक्ति को देखो: आज वह मर गया, कल वह जीवित था।
english: The grey one has swallowed the young, solitary one, running in the gathering of many. Behold the wisdom of the god: today he has died, yesterday he lived.
notes: vidhuṃ is tentative (lone one; some read 'moon'). samane could be 'gathering' or 'battle'. The verse is a riddle; no interpretation is imported. samāna is read sam-āna (sam-√an 'breathed').

words.gram: pres. part. pass., m. nom. sg.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, उत्पन्न होते ही तुम बिना शत्रु वाले सातों के लिए शत्रु बने। छिपे हुए द्यावा-पृथिवी को तुमने पाया, और व्यापक लोकों को आनन्द दिया।
english: You, O Indra, being born, became a foe for the seven who had no foe. You found Heaven and Earth hidden, and gave delight to the pervading worlds.
notes: 'the seven' is not explained in the verse. raṇam is rendered 'delight' (it can also be 'battle'). jāyamāno'śatrubhyo is jāyamānaḥ aśatrubhyaḥ.

hindi: मैं तुम्हारी स्तुति करता हूँ, खम्भे के समान दृढ़, वज्रधारी, नुकीले अस्त्रों वाले, अनेक दानों वाले, दृढ़ देह वाले बैल की; हे इन्द्र, आकाशीय वृत्रहन्ता, सेवा चाहने वाले स्वामी, तुम बलवानों को अपना बनाते हो।
english: I praise you, the wielder of the thunderbolt, spiked, of many (gifts), the bull firm of body, firm like a post, O Indra, heavenly slayer of Vṛtra; eager to serve, you make the strong ones (yours).
notes: Line 2 is obscure: aryaḥ and taruṣīḥ are uncertain, and the exact construction of karoṣi aryaḥ taruṣīḥ duvasyuḥ is not clear. purudhasmānam is tentative. Needs review.

words.gloss: filling the peoples, fulfiller of men

hindi: तुम सब उस महान, अत्यन्त बढ़ाने वाले और बुद्धिमान के लिए स्तुति लाओ और उसके प्रति अच्छी बुद्धि प्रकट करो। हे मनुष्यों को पूर्ण करने वाले, तुम बहुतेरी प्रजाओं के बीच आगे बढ़ो।
english: Bring praise forth for the great one who makes great, the wise one, and show forth good will to him. Go forth among the many peoples, O fulfiller of men.
notes: The first line has no object printed; 'praise' is supplied in the translation as the natural object of bharadhvam (an addition to complete the sense). Line 2 has only four words (a short third pada); this is normal for the metre. The god addressed is not named. carṣaṇiprāḥ may be vocative or nominative.

words.gloss: in the winning of the prize

hindi: कल्याण के लिए हम धनवान इन्द्र को पुकारें, इस युद्ध में सबसे वीर को, पुरस्कार जीतने में; सुनने वाले, उग्र को सहायता के लिए, युद्धों में शत्रुओं को मारने वाले और धनों को जीतने वाले को।
english: For prosperity may we call the bountiful Indra, in this battle, the most manly, in the winning of the prize; the hearing one, the mighty, for help, smiting the foes in the battles, conqueror of prizes.

text_flags.why: possible: the participle of √han is ghnantam; dhn- looks like a typing/reading error for ghn-.

notes: śuna~ is śunam (anunāsika for m), here 'for prosperity' (it can also be an adverb, 'well'). maghavānam is the accusative of maghavan.

words.gram: m. voc. sg. (name of a sage)

hindi: प्रार्थनाएँ यश की चाह से उठाई गई हैं; हे वसिष्ठ, युद्ध में इन्द्र का सम्मान करो। जिसने यश से सब कुछ फैला दिया है, वह मेरे इतने वचनों का सुनने वाला हो।
english: Prayers, eager for fame, have been raised up; honour Indra in the contest, O Vasiṣṭha. He who has stretched out over all things with fame, let him be the hearer of these my words.
notes: ma īvato is read me īvataḥ; īvataḥ ('so many') and its agreement are uncertain. upaśrotā is rendered as a wish ('let him be the hearer'). The addressee of mahayā is the sage Vasiṣṭha named in the line.

hindi: उसका जो चक्र जलों में स्थित है, वह मधु ही उसके लिए ढके; पृथ्वी पर जो ऊधस् उँडेला गया, उसके दूध को तुमने गायों में और पौधों में रखा।
english: The wheel of his that is seated in the waters, and that sweetness indeed, may it shelter him; the milk of the udder poured out on the earth you placed in the cows and in the plants.
notes: The verse is obscure. cakra is kept as 'wheel' (it can be 'disc'); cacchadyāt (√chad 'cover') and atiṣitam are uncertain; the link of line 1 to line 2 is not clear, and ūdhaḥ payaḥ may be read together as 'the milk of the udder'. Tentative; needs review.

hindi: हम कल्याण के लिए यहाँ उस वेगवान, देवताओं से प्रेरित, बलवान, रथों को पीछे छोड़ने वाले, अटूट पहिये की पुट्ठी वाले, युद्ध में जीतने वाले, तीव्र तार्क्ष्य को पुकारें।
english: May we call here, for well-being, that swift Tārkṣya, urged by the gods, mighty, overtaker of chariots, with unharmed felly, winning in battle, fast.
notes: Tārkṣya is kept as a name; the verse gives no identification and none is imported. ariṣṭanemi: nemi is the rim (felly) of a wheel.

hindi: रक्षक इन्द्र को, सहायक इन्द्र को, हर पुकार पर सहज बुलाए जाने वाले, शूर इन्द्र को; मैं अब शक्तिमान, बहुतों से पुकारे गए इन्द्र को बुलाता हूँ। धनवान इन्द्र इस हवि को स्वीकार करे।
english: Indra the protector, Indra the helper, at every call Indra easy to call, the hero Indra; I now call the mighty Śakra, much-invoked Indra. May the bountiful Indra enjoy this oblation.
notes: Anunāsika spellings (indra~, suhava~, ida~) are read as -m. The first line is a run of accusatives governed by huve in line 2.

words.gram: 1 pl. pres. mid. √yaj (e before a vowel)

words.gloss: with the thunderbolt in the right hand
with the beard, with the whiskers

words.gram: pres. part. mid., m. nom. sg. (uncertain)

hindi: हम दाहिने हाथ में वज्र रखने वाले इन्द्र की पूजा करते हैं, जो भिन्न इच्छाओं वाले हरे घोड़ों का रथ-चालक है। दाढ़ी-मूँछ हिलाता हुआ वह ऊपर उठाने वाला हुआ; सेनाओं से वह भय फैलाता है और अपनी उदारता से अलग-अलग देता है।
english: We worship Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his right hand, the charioteer of the diverse-willed bay horses. Shaking forth with his beard, he has become the one who raises up; he spreads fear with his armies, and with his bounty (gives) apart.
notes: The second line is obscure: ūrdhvadhā, bhayamānaḥ and the two vi are uncertain, and the second vi has no clear verb; the translation is tentative and needs review. The 3 in rathya3ṃ is a pluta mark in the chant, placed after rathyam. The anunāsika forms (dakṣiṇa~, harīṇā~) are read as -m.

hindi: शत्रुओं का सदा नाश करने वाले, साहसी, प्रबल, महान, अपार, उत्तम वज्र वाले बैल इन्द्र को; जो वृत्र का हन्ता, वाज का विजेता, धनों का दाता, मघवान और उदार है।
english: Indra, the constant slayer, the bold, the thrusting, great and boundless, the bull with the fine thunderbolt; who is the slayer of Vṛtra, the winner of the prize, the giver of gifts, the bountiful, of good bounty.

text_flags.why: possible: ś for ṣ looks like a typing error; the word is vṛṣabha 'bull'.

notes: tumram is tentative (thrusting, strong). The glossary sets vājam 'prize/strength'; rendered 'prize' here.

words.gram: pres. part. mid., m. nom. sg.

hindi: जो मनुष्य हमें हानि पहुँचाना चाहता हुआ हम पर टूटता है, चाहे वह स्वयं को उग्र या शीघ्र मानता हो, हे इन्द्र, उसे युद्ध से या बल से दबा दो। तुम्हारी सहायता से पुरुषार्थी हम उस पर भारी पड़ें।
english: The mortal who, seeking to harm us, attacks us, thinking himself fierce or swift, him, O Indra, overpower by fight or by might; may we prevail over him, manly-minded and helped by you.

text_flags.why: possible: ugaṇā is not a clear word; ugraṇā (fierceness) or ugra 'mighty' + a particle fits the metre and sense.

notes: kṣidhī is unclear ('overpower' by context); ugaṇā is unresolved (see text_flags). The relative clause yo ... martaḥ is picked up by tam.

words.gram: pres. part. mid., m. nom. pl.
pres. part. caus., m. nom. pl.

words.gloss: at the foot, in the rush

hindi: जिसे विरोधी बनकर लड़ने वाली प्रजाएँ शत्रुओं के बीच पुकारती हैं, जिसे जुते हुए रथों में शीघ्रता करने वाले पुकारते हैं; जिसे शूरों की विजय में, जिसे जलों के निकट, जिसे प्रेरित ऋषि पुरस्कार के लिए पुकारते हैं, वही इन्द्र है।
english: He whom the peoples, contending in the battles with foes, call upon, whom those hastening in the yoked teams call upon; whom in the winning of heroes, whom at the rush of the waters, whom the inspired sages seek the prize by, he is Indra.

text_flags.why: possible: the final visarga is not printed before spardhamānā; the form is kṣitayaḥ (nom. pl.).

notes: ya~ is yam (anunāsika for m). upajmanyaṃ is read upajmani + yam; the sense of upajman (foot, rush) is uncertain. vājayante is taken as 'strive for the prize' with the preceding yam as the object of invocation.

hindi: हे इन्द्र और पर्वत, अपने विशाल रथ से सुन्दर, वीरों वाले अन्न लाओ; हे देवो, यज्ञों में हवियों का सेवन करो, और स्तुतियों तथा इडा से आनन्दित होकर बढ़ो।
english: O Indra and Parvata, bring with your great chariot lovely refreshments rich in heroes. O gods, enjoy the oblations in the rites, and grow strong, rejoicing in songs and the offering.
notes: Parvata ('mountain') is kept as a name of a god paired with Indra; the line gives no more. iḍā is rendered 'offering' (it is also the name of a goddess).

words.gloss: of the reservoir, of the ocean

hindi: इन्द्र के लिए अनथक बहने वाली स्तुतियाँ हैं; उसने समुद्र की गहराई से जलों को चलाया, जिसने अपनी शक्तियों से पृथ्वी और आकाश को अलग-अलग थाम दिया, जैसे धुरी दो पहियों को।
english: For Indra are the songs of unchecked outpouring; he set the waters in motion from the depth of the reservoir, who propped Earth and Heaven apart by his powers, as an axle does two wheels.
notes: sagarasya is rendered 'reservoir' (it may mean 'ocean'). The relative clause yo ... is attached to Indra; aniśitasargāḥ is taken as an epithet of giraḥ.

words.gram: pres. part. mid., m. nom. sg.

hindi: मित्र अपनी मित्रता से तुम्हें इधर मोड़ लाएँ, चाहे तुम बहुत सी बाढ़ों को पार करके आओ। ज्ञानी इस निवास में आगे चमकते हुए पिता के वंशज को स्थापित करे।
english: May your friends turn you hither by friendship, though you traverse many floods. May the wise one establish in this dwelling the descendant of the father, shining forth further.
notes: pituḥ napātam is rendered 'the descendant of the father' (it can also be 'grandson'); who is meant is not stated. The line break between lines 1 and 2 follows the printed lines.

words.gloss: to the pole, in the yoke

hindi: आज ऋत की उन तेजस्वी, क्रोधी और कठिनता से शान्त होने वाली गायों को जुए में कौन जोतता है? जो इन आनन्ददायकों की सेवा पूरी करता है, वह जीवित रहे।
english: Who today yokes to the pole the cows of the order, the energetic, fiery, hard-to-appease ones? Whoever accomplishes their service, the joy-bringing ones? He who accomplishes their service shall live.
notes: Line 2 is obscure and corrupt-looking: āsan eṣām apsuvāhaḥ mayobhūn is uncertain (compare the Ṛgveda mouth-and-arrows wording), and the translation of that part is tentative. The 'cows' are not identified.
